For WP 7.1 there will be a new Attached images category in the media inserter tab to allow folks to view, select, attach and detach attached media. See:

* https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/79336
* https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/76955
* https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/77117

However, this work reveals that there is much that can be improved in the media inserter and it could be worth overhauling the inserter for WP 7.2+ and beyond. Here is an idea shared by @fcoveram in https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/79217#issuecomment-4777334475

This issue is for discussing future ideas for the media inserter. For issues related to the new category that will be introduced in WP 7.1, see #77117.

### A Concept

From @fcoveram: Prototype: [https://prototypes.fvm.house/media-tab-inserter-concept/](https://prototypes.fvm.house/media-tab-inserter-concept/)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7f825fd-8778-472b-8a26-1f70251645bc

> The idea involves the following:
> 
> - There are three panels in the Media tab for searching, managing, and inserting media content: Quick access to media content, Full access to Media Library, and search on the web (powered by Openverse).
> - The quick access area is called "Pinned" (name TBD) as the content is not really inserted or attached to the document, neither to the canvas nor at the meta level, such as featured image. Therefore, I'm drawn to use a term that refers to the handy condition rather than it's role into the document.
> - Media library shows all content where each can be pinned.
> - Searching on the web shows the current suggested content and each can be added to the Media Library.
> - In all panels, the search and settings menu allows to filter per content type and potentially include options, like layout settings.

### Issues to address / discuss in addition to the above

Elsewhere the following feedback and suggestions have been raised, which should be incorporated into any designs or ideas:

* There is an open core/trac issue for adding media folders and categorisation for media. How should this inserter look when users can easily add their own categories and folders. I.e. we will need to at least expose these categories here, but we might also add the ability to _create_ folders from this view
* Showing images in their actual aspect ratio: some folks have flagged that they'd like to be able to see the image in its real aspect ratio before insertion so that they can tell if they've got a 16:9 or a 9:16 image, rather than just selecting from a square
* How can we handle pagination in this UI? Imagine a long-lived site that has thousands of images
* Any other issues / things to keep in mind for this sidebar?
resources.title: Discussion: How might the media inserter tab look in WP 7.2+

We would like to be able to disable the entire new "Media" tab of the Block Inserter, introduced in 6.1.

We were able to get rid of the OpenVerse category through the code snippet provided here ( https://make.wordpress.org/core/2023/03/07/miscellaneous-editor-changes-in-wordpress-6-2/ ), but would love to disable the entire tab.

The primary reason we're trying to remove is because it's called "Media", but doesn't include everything from the Media Library. Our content providers use a LOT of pdfs and other documents, which one would expect to be here, as it's in the "media library". When these things aren't there, it's a poor user experience.

It's made even worse by the fact that the tab includes a button to open the Media Library... but it opens a view of it that is silently filtered to only include images (again, not PDFs or other files). There is zero indication on the screen that this is only showing Image files.  If you tab over to "Upload Files" and add a pdf (which probably shouldn't even be possible), the upload succeeds, but the newly uploaded file isn't visible, again because the screen is silently filtering to only show Images.
resources.title: Allow new "Media" tab of the Block Inserter to be disabled

resources.body: Related: #43241 ## What? Adds fit text support to the Poetry block. ## Why? The Poetry block supports font size, line height, text alignment, colour, background, border, shadow, spacing and minimum dimensions, but has no fit text control. Heading, Paragraph, Site Title and Site Tagline have it. This brings Poetry in line as part of the design tools consistency work. ## How? Adds `typography.fitText` to the block's `block.json` supports. Fit text is applied by the `@wordpress/block-editor/utils/fit-text-frontend` script module at runtime rather than by CSS: it sizes the block to the space available and resizes it when the container changes. While it is on, it supersedes the block's other typography values. Fit text's shared `.has-fit-text` rule sets `white-space: nowrap`, which collapses the leading spaces poetry uses for indentation. A rule in the block's `style.scss` switches that to `white-space: pre` for Poetry, which keeps the spacing and the line breaks and still stops lines wrapping, so the longest line sets the size. The editor needs nothing extra: the same rule overrides the inline `pre-wrap` rich text sets. The core blocks reference and the block's `README.md` are regenerated to list `fitText`. ## Testing Instructions Setup: a post with a Poetry block holding a short stanza, with some lines indented by a few spaces. 1. Fit text off: the stanza renders as before. 2. Typography panel: turn on Fit text. - Editor and front end: the longest line fills the block's width. - Shorter lines keep their size relative to it, and indentation and line breaks are kept. 3. Front end at a mobile width. - The stanza scales down so the longest line still fits. 4. Resize the container, for example by narrowing the browser window or putting the block in a narrow column. - The size updates to fit. 5. Pick a font size: Fit text turns off. 6. With JavaScript disabled, the block renders at whatever size CSS gives it, since fit text is set by a script module. A known, pre-existing bug: in the editor's Mobile responsive view, the inspector hides Fit text but still shows Font size, and a mobile font size then wins on the front end while the editor still shows fit text. Site Title on trunk does the same. It is not caused by this change. ## Screenshots or screencast ## Use of AI Tools Implemented, built and screenshotted by a Claude Code agent from a predefined task.

resources.body: Fixes responsive and pseudo-state block values doing nothing on List Item, in the editor and on the front end. ## What? Scopes per-instance state rules to the element the instance class is on, when a block's selector starts with a different block's class. ## Why? List Item declares `"root": ".wp-block-list > li"`. The instance class goes on the `li`, but the rule swapped the leading `.wp-block-list` for it. That gives `.wp-states-xxxx > li`, which asks for an `li` inside the list item and matches nothing. So a List Item mobile value for colour, background, typography, spacing or border is inert today. Global Styles and the desktop block value already work. Found while adding background support to List Item. ## How? A leading compound is treated as an ancestor only when: - it is a `wp-block-*` class that is not this block's own, derived from the block name, and - the compound after it carries no `wp-block-*` class of its own. Then the ancestor and its combinator are kept, and the next compound is swapped for the instance class. Everything else keeps today's leading swap. | Block selector | Scoped result | | --- | --- | | `.wp-block-list > li` (List Item) | `.wp-block-list > .wp-states-xxxx` | | `.wp-block-list:not(.wp-block-list .wp-block-list) > li` (List Item border) | `.wp-block-list:not(.wp-block-list .wp-block-list) > .wp-states-xxxx` | | `.wp-block-search .wp-block-search__input` | `.wp-states-xxxx .wp-block-search__input`, as today | | `.wp-block-button .wp-block-button__link` | `.wp-states-xxxx .wp-block-button__link`, as today | The ancestor is kept rather than dropped, so the state rule matches the same element as the non-state rule and keeps the same specificity. The same logic lives on both sides: `gutenberg_build_state_selector()` in `lib/block-supports/states.php`, and `buildScopedBlockSelector()` in `packages/block-editor/src/hooks/state-utils.js`. Both now get the block name. No new API or `block.json` field. Blocks covered: List Item, for its root selector, its border selector and responsive element styles. Button, Icon, Table, Paragraph, Search and every other library selector are unchanged, since their leading compound is the block's own class or not a `wp-block-*` class at all. One edge: a third-party block that borrows another block's class as its root, with a bare element after it, would now be read as an ancestor. ## Testing Instructions Setup: a List with three items. On the middle one set a background colour, then the same with Mobile selected (View > Responsive styles > Mobile) in a different colour. 1. List Item background: desktop value at desktop width, mobile value at mobile width. - Editor: switch the preview to Mobile. - Front end: resize below 480px. 2. Repeat with text colour on a List Item. Same result. 3. Paragraph with desktop and mobile background values. Unchanged, both apply at their own widths. 4. Button with a hover background. Hovering the link shows it, in the editor and on the front end. 5. Global Styles and Global Styles mobile values for List Item and Paragraph. Unchanged. Unit tests: `phpunit/block-supports/states-test.php` and `packages/block-editor/src/hooks/test/state-utils.js`. ## Screenshots or screencast ## Use of AI Tools Implemented, built and screenshotted by a Claude Code agent from a predefined task.

resources.body: ## What Adds minimum width and minimum height support to the Post Navigation Link block. ## Why Post Navigation Link already has border, shadow and spacing, so it is often styled as a button or a small card, but there is no way to give it a minimum size. Part of the design tools consistency work: #43241 ## How `dimensions.minWidth` and `dimensions.minHeight` are added to `block.json`. The block renders an empty wrapper when there is no adjacent post. Border, shadow and spacing already handle that (#83058, #83122), and dimensions follows the same three parts so a minimum size never paints an empty box: - `dimensions.__experimentalSkipSerialization`, so the dimensions block support does not inject styles onto the wrapper. - `block_core_post_navigation_link_get_support_styles()` now also generates the `min-width` and `min-height` styles. They are applied only when a link renders. - A `selectors.dimensions` entry of `.wp-block-post-navigation-link:not(:empty)`, so Global Styles skip the empty wrapper too. The editor applies the styles through `getDimensionsClassesAndStyles()`, next to the existing border, shadow and spacing props. The editor always renders the link, so for an empty block the editor shows the minimum size and the front end does not. That matches border, shadow and spacing. PHP tests cover the empty wrapper and a rendered link. The generated docs are regenerated. In the screenshots the tinted card, the narrow content column and the outlined paragraph after the block are a capture aid, not part of the change: a minimum size paints nothing on its own. ## Testing instructions Use a post that has an older post before it, so the link renders. Add a Post Navigation Link block set to Previous. Check each state in the editor and on the front end. 1. **No styles.** The block renders as before. 2. **Global Styles.** In Styles, open Blocks, then Post Navigation Link, then Dimensions. Set Minimum width `300px` and Minimum height `140px`, and save. The block shows both in the editor and on the front end. 3. **Responsive Global Styles.** With step 2 still applied, open the View menu, then Responsive styles, then Mobile. Set Minimum width `250px` and Minimum height `100px` for the block in Styles, and save. The mobile preview and the front end at a mobile width show the mobile values. The desktop width keeps the step 2 values. 4. **Block overrides Global Styles.** Back on Desktop, select the block and set Minimum width `560px` and Minimum height `340px` under Dimensions in the block inspector. Save. The block values win in the editor and on the front end at every width, mobile included, because a block value outranks the Global Styles mobile value from step 3. 5. **Block value with Mobile selected.** With step 4 still applied, select Mobile in the View menu, then set Minimum width `300px` and Minimum height `240px` on the block. resources.body: Related: #43241 ## What? Adds border support (colour, radius, style and width) to the Site Logo block. ## Why? Site Logo has spacing and duotone, but no way to frame the logo. The block already carries a radius through its Rounded style variation, so a border control is the natural next step. ## How? Adds `__experimentalBorder` to the block's `block.json`, with no default controls, matching the other recent border adoptions. The border lands on the block wrapper. The render callback returns an empty string when no logo is set, so there is never an empty bordered box. The generated docs do not change, because the docs generators skip `__experimental` keys. The wrapper is a block level `div`, so in a plain flow layout the border spans the content width rather than hugging the image, the same as padding does today. Inside a Row, or with left or right alignment, it wraps the logo. ## Testing Instructions Setup: set a site logo (Settings > General or the block's own upload). resources.body: ## What Adds background gradient support to the Search block. ## Why Search already has colour, border, typography and spacing tools, but its only gradient comes from the legacy `color.gradients` support. The newer `background` support lets a gradient set values per breakpoint. Part of the design tools consistency work: #43241 ## How Search skips colour serialization and paints colour on the search button, or on the input when there is no button. The gradient has to land on the same element, so: - `block.json` adds `background.gradient` with `background.__experimentalSkipSerialization`, so nothing lands on the wrapper, and a `selectors.background` entry matching the colour selector so Global Styles and responsive block values target the same element. - Editor: `edit.jsx` applies `useBackgroundProps()` to the button, or to the input with no button, next to the colour props. - Front end: the background block support bails when serialization is skipped, so `styles_for_block_core_search()` passes the gradient to the style engine and adds the result to the same element as the colour, and `has-background` follows it. `color.gradients` stays, since it is a shipped control and removing it needs its own change. Background image and size are left out on purpose: an image behind a search field sits under the typed text and hurts legibility. No deprecation is needed. Search is dynamic, and existing posts carry no background attribute, so their markup is unchanged. ## Testing instructions Add a Search block to a post. Check each state in the editor and on the front end. 1. **No styles.** The block renders as before, with no gradient. 2. **Global Styles.** In Styles, open Blocks, then Search, then Background. ## What?

Adds a developer opt-in filter, `wp_generate_animated_image_subsizes`, that re-enables animated (multi-frame) sub-size generation for animated GIFs in the client-side media processing pipeline:

```php
add_filter( 'wp_generate_animated_image_subsizes', '__return_true' );
```

Fixes https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/80383.
Also fixes the 12-year-old core request [Trac #28474 - "WordPress destroys animation in animated GIF when it resizes"](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/28474), as proposed in [comment:58](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/28474#comment:58).

Core backport: [Trac #65656](https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/65656) / WordPress/wordpress-develop#12572.

> [!NOTE]
> Stacked on #80268, which makes static first-frame sub-sizes the default. This PR adds the opt-in path back on top of it. Only the last commit is new; review the diff from `fix/animated-gif-subsize-performance`.

## Why?

#80268 switched sub-sizes of animated GIFs to static first-frame images, matching what WordPress core has always done server-side, because full animated re-encodes were extremely expensive (~88 s combined for a 769-frame GIF, with sub-sizes larger than the original - see #80266).

But there is long-standing, sustained demand for resized GIFs that keep their animation: Trac #28474 has been open since 2014 and stalled server-side because GD cannot do it and Imagick is only available on a subset of hosts. Client-side processing sidesteps both constraints - the cost is paid once in the uploading user's browser, and wasm-vips is available regardless of host configuration. That makes animated sub-sizes reasonable as an explicit developer opt-in while keeping the fast, core-consistent static behavior as the default.

## How?

The flag follows the exact same path as `image_strip_meta` / `image_max_bit_depth` (#80218):

1. **PHP** (`lib/media/load.php`): `wp_generate_animated_image_subsizes` (boolean, default `false`) is applied in `gutenberg_media_processing_filter_rest_index()` and exposed as `animated_image_subsizes` on the REST API root index. The field is also added to the preload/entities field lists (`lib/compat/wordpress-7.1/preload.php`, `packages/core-data/src/entities.js`), which must match exactly.
2. **Editor settings**: mapped to a `generateAnimatedImageSubsizes` setting in `use-block-editor-settings.js` and forwarded by `use-media-upload-settings.js`.
3. **Upload pipeline**: `resizeCropItem` reads the setting from the `@wordpress/upload-media` store and passes it to the vips worker as a new `preserveAnimation` option on `resizeImage()` (options object from #80328).
4. **Vips**: when `preserveAnimation` is set and the resize is uncropped, `resizeImage()` restores the pre-#80268 `[n=-1]` load path so all frames are decoded and re-encoded. Cropped sizes (e.g. `thumbnail`) always flatten to the first frame, matching the pre-existing behavior - per-frame smart-cropping is out of scope.

### Tuned `gifsave` settings

The profiling in #80266 showed ~85% of the animated resize cost is GIF re-encoding (per-frame palette quantization), and that default `gifsave` settings cause the output-larger-than-input bloat. When writing an animated GIF, this PR applies the settings benchmarked there:

- `effort: 2`, `interframe_maxerror: 8`, `interpalette_maxerror: 16` - measured 4-8x faster and eliminates the size bloat.

That turns the opt-in cost from ~88 s into roughly 10-20 s for a very large GIF - still too slow to be the default, but a reasonable trade for a site that has explicitly chosen animated sub-sizes.

### Notes

- The filter name says "animated image", not "GIF", deliberately: vips can also preserve frames for animated WebP, and APNG has come up on the Trac ticket. This implementation is exercised with GIFs; the door is open.
- Core's `wp_calculate_image_srcset()` still never mixes the full-size GIF and its sub-sizes in one `srcset`. With animated sub-sizes that guard becomes overly conservative but harmless; relaxing it is a server-side follow-up.
- Server-side uploads (Media Library taking the server path) still produce static sub-sizes, so enabling the filter reintroduces a difference between upload surfaces - this time as an explicit developer choice. Documented on the filter.
- Guardrail interplay with #80376 (timeout/pixel budgets, falling back to a static sub-size) is a follow-up once #80379 lands.

## Testing Instructions

[![Test in WordPress Playground](https://img.shields.io/badge/Test%20in-WordPress%20Playground-3858e9?logo=wordpress&logoColor=white)](https://playground.wordpress.net/gutenberg.html?pr=80385)

1. Enable the filter, e.g. in a mu-plugin: `add_filter( 'wp_generate_animated_image_subsizes', '__return_true' );`
2. In the block editor, upload an animated GIF to an Image block and wait for the upload to finish.
3. Inspect the attachment's `medium` / `large` sub-sizes (e.g. via `/wp-json/wp/v2/media/<id>`): they should be animated GIFs (multiple frames), while `thumbnail` (cropped) remains a static first frame.
4. Without the filter, all sub-sizes remain static first-frame images (the #80268 default), and the existing e2e test covers this.

### Documentation

The client-side media docs ([#75895](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/75895)) are updated alongside: the how-to guide gains an "Animated image sub-sizes" section for the new filter, and the architecture reference adds it to the filter table and REST index field list (plus corrects the now-stale note that sub-sizes preserve all frames).

### Automated tests

- `packages/vips/src/test/resize-image.ts`: new `preserveAnimation` suite - `[n=-1]` + tuned gifsave for uncropped animated resizes, first-frame flattening for crops, no effect on still formats.
- `phpunit/media/media-processing-test.php`: REST index exposes `generate_animated_image_subsizes` (default `false`, honors the filter, hidden without `upload_files`).
- `test/e2e/specs/editor/various/gif-to-video.spec.js`: new test uploads an animated GIF with the filter enabled (via a new e2e test plugin) and asserts the `medium` sub-size keeps all frames.

```bash
npm run test:unit packages/vips/src/test/
vendor/bin/phpunit phpunit/media/media-processing-test.php
npm run test:e2e -- test/e2e/specs/editor/various/gif-to-video.spec.js
```

Existing posts carry no background attribute, so their saved markup and `save` output are unchanged. The generated docs are regenerated: the core blocks reference and the block's own `README.md` both now list the new supports. ## Testing instructions Add a Paragraph block with a few lines of text to a post. Check each state in the editor and on the front end. 1. **No styles.** The paragraph renders as before, with no background image or gradient. 2. **Global Styles.** In Styles, open Blocks, then Paragraph, then Background. Set an image, a size (for example Cover) and a gradient, and save. The paragraph shows all three in the editor and on the front end. 3. **Responsive Global Styles.** With step 2 still applied, open the View menu, then Responsive styles, then Mobile. In Styles, open Blocks, then Paragraph, then Background, and set a different size and gradient. Save. The mobile preview shows the mobile values, and so does the front end at a mobile width, while the desktop width keeps the step 2 values. 4. **Block overrides Global Styles.** Back on Desktop, select the Paragraph block and set a different image, a size (for example Contain) and a gradient under Background in the block inspector. Save. The block level values win in the editor and on the front end at every width, mobile included, because a block value outranks the Global Styles mobile value from step 3. 5. **Block value with Mobile selected.** With step 4 still applied, select Mobile in the View menu, then set a different size and gradient on the block. Save. The mobile preview and the front end at a mobile width show these values, while the desktop width keeps the step 4 values. 6. **Same box as the colour.** Set a background colour on the block alongside the image and gradient. ## What?

Adds Restore original image to the media editor's More options menu. UI for the lineage data from #81803.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64c915e3-6ec1-4c4d-ac5a-af7d75cefa8a

Part of #78077. Supersedes #77781.

> [!NOTE]
> Based on #81803. Retarget to trunk after #81803 merges.

## Why?

A cropped image should offer a way back to its original without hunting for it in the media library.

## How?

The action appears in More options when the attachment exposes a root-level `edit_root` id (see #81803). It discards pending edits and loads the original image and its editable details. Keyboard shortcuts also move into More options for all images.

- Save without further edits: the block points at the original again. No attachment write.
- Edit details without cropping: update the original attachment.
- Crop, then save: a new image is created from the original, not from the crop.
- Cancel discards the restore.
- In the experimental media editor route (including site editor v2), Restore then Save opens the original; the edited attachment remains unchanged.
- Failed details saves show an error and keep the editor open for retry.
- An explicit Undo callback replaces #82829’s Image-only detection, restoring Image metadata, size and links, and Cover size and automatic overlay while preserving later dim/overlay changes and recalculating contrast. Site Logo uses the ID fallback.

## Test plan

1. Upload an image, crop or rotate it in the media editor, save.
2. Reopen the edited image in the media editor. More options shows Restore original image.
3. Click it, save. The block shows the original and no new attachment is created.
4. Repeat, editing details without cropping: the original is updated. Then try cropping: a new image is created from the original.
5. Click Restore, then cancel. The discard confirmation appears.
6. Open an image that was never edited. No restore action.
7. Use snackbar Undo in Image, Cover and Site Logo, including before Save finishes updating the block and after changing Cover dim/overlay.
8. Fail a details save: the error appears, edits remain, and retry succeeds.

## Follow ups

In-modal restore undo/redo remains a follow-up:

> When you set a new image on the canvas it clears the history stack, we need to record how an image is loaded, or at least a `RESTORE_SOURCE` action. With that in the history, we'd get undo/redo.

If a block has no settings or styles tabs (for example, paragraph only has style controls) then there are now Additional styles and Advanced panels that group the controls, both appear in the one inspector. ## Why? I've noticed for a while that the block inspector shows 'Additional CSS' and 'Apply Globally' (Push to Global Styles) in the Settings tab, and I this this could be improved. These are more 'Styles' tools than 'Settings'. 'Apply Globally' is one that's problematic to me, as users are likely to use this when having just modified styles. Users have to switch to the settings tab, scroll down, expand the 'Advanced' panel and then click the button, and then probably switch back to the Styles tab. It's a lot of context switching. ## How? Introduces a new 'additional-styles' inspector group specifically for styles controls. Renames 'Additional CSS Class(es)', 'Additional CSS' to 'CSS Class(es)' and 'CSS'. Renames the global styles 'Advanced' panel to 'Additional styles'. ## Testing Instructions 1. Add a paragraph block 2. Open the block inspector 3. Observe there's an 'Additional styles' panel for style controls and 'Advanced' panel for tools 4. Add a Media Text block 5. Open the block inspector 6. resources.body: ## Summary Closes [#78188](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/78188). With Suggest mode making review notes effectively free (every edit becomes a note), the manual **Add note** action no longer belongs at the bottom of the block toolbar's overflow menu. This PR promotes it to a first-class toolbar button — a speech-bubble icon placed just before the ellipsis — so it sits at parity with Suggest mode's automatic note creation. ### Behavior - **Block with no thread** → the new `Add note` toolbar button appears (speech-bubble icon). - **Block with a thread** → the existing `NoteAvatarIndicator` continues to appear (participant avatars). Only one notes affordance is shown at a time, avoiding visual clutter. - **Distraction-free / view mode / unsupported post types** → unchanged (no affordance). - **Keyboard shortcut** (`primaryAlt+M`) → unchanged. ## Testing [![Test in WordPress Playground](https://img.shields.io/badge/Test_in-WP_Playground-blue?style=for-the-badge&logo=wordpress)](https://playground.wordpress.net/gutenberg.html?pr=78205) ### Implementation - Replace `add-note-menu-item.js` (MenuItem in `NoteIconSlotFill`) with `add-note-toolbar-button.js` (ToolbarButton in `NoteIconToolbarSlotFill`). - Remove the now-unused `NoteIconSlotFill` slot from `block-settings-dropdown` and unregister the private API. - Update `NotesSidebar` to render the new toolbar button only when the selected block has no thread (mirrors the avatar-indicator branch). - Update e2e specs (`block-notes.spec.js`, `collaboration-notes.spec.ts`) to click the toolbar button instead of opening the overflow menu. ### Design decisions (from the issue's open questions) 1. **Zero notes vs. always**: only render when block has zero notes — `NoteAvatarIndicator` already handles the "open notes" affordance for threaded blocks. 2. **Every block vs. opt-in**: same gating as today's menu item (post-type `editor.notes` support, valid + registered, not classic). 3. **View mode**: unchanged — entire sidebar is already hidden. 4. **Mobile/narrow**: render in toolbar (matches existing `NoteAvatarIndicator` pattern). ## Screenshot ## Test plan - [ ] Insert a paragraph; confirm the speech-bubble **Add note** button appears in the block toolbar just before the ellipsis. - [ ] Click the button → New-note form opens and is focused. - [ ] Save a note → button is replaced by the avatar indicator on that block. - [ ] Insert a second paragraph (no note) → speech-bubble button appears again. - [ ] Toggle distraction-free mode → no Add note button surfaces. - [ ] Classic block → button is disabled with a "Convert to blocks to add notes." tooltip. - [ ] Keyboard shortcut `primaryAlt+M` still opens the new-note form. - [ ] Run `test/e2e/specs/editor/various/block-notes.spec.js` and `test/e2e/specs/editor/collaboration/collaboration-notes.spec.ts`. ## Related - Tracking: [#73411](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/73411) - Suggest mode direction: [#73410](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/73410) - Origin discussion: [PR #77403 review thread](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/77403#issuecomment-4418252859) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added an accessible “Add note” button to the block toolbar. * The button now toggles the note form and updates its expanded state. * Added a fade-in transition for floating note cards, respecting reduced-motion preferences. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved note controls for editable blocks and distraction-free mode. * Updated keyboard navigation to include the “Add note” toolbar control. * **Tests** * Updated collaboration and block-note tests to use the toolbar button and verify toggle behavior.

An alternate take on #78176, so the two approaches can be compared side by side. Standalone against trunk: includes the changes from #76767 (previously stacked on it).

Fixes https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/75144

To keep this one reviewable, the filters for customizing the emoji set, exclusions, and labels moved to a stacked follow-up, #84043.

This round addresses the feedback from @mirka and @fcoveram. The picker now follows the documented `Autocomplete` patterns without patching the component's behavior, and the rough edges we hit are collected below under "Autocomplete notes" to pass back.

_Claude reworked the picker and wrote up the changes:_

> ## What?
>
> Rebuilds the Notes full emoji picker from #78176 on the Design System `Autocomplete` primitive from `@wordpress/ui`, in its `grid` mode (inline, always open), instead of the `Composite` grid plus `SearchControl` from `@wordpress/components`.
>
> ## Why?
>
> Addresses @fcoveram's keyboard feedback on #78176: getting from the search field to the grid took several Tab presses. With `Autocomplete` the search field is a `combobox` that drives the grid through `aria-activedescendant`, which is the macOS behavior from the review:
>
> - focus stays in the search field
> - the arrow keys move a highlight through the grid, crossing category boundaries
> - Enter picks the highlighted emoji
> - after typing, the top result is highlighted, so type + Enter picks it
> - one Tab reaches the skin-tone button
>
> ## How?
>
> - Every reaction, including the five quick ones, is stored as its Emojibase hex key (`2764`, `1f680`), and `reaction_summary` is keyed the same way. The server accepts a valid hex key and nothing else.
> - If the Emojibase data cannot load, the picker shows "Couldn't load emojis." instead of falling back to the quick reactions.
> - Composed like the documented async items story (https://wordpress.github.io/gutenberg/?path=/docs/design-system-components-form-primitives-autocomplete--docs#async-items): the results go to `Autocomplete.Root` through `items`, and `Autocomplete.Status` and `Autocomplete.Empty` handle the loading state, the result count, and the empty state. The list stays mounted.
> - `filter={ null }` instead of `mode="none"`, so `aria-autocomplete` stays accurate. Filtering is still ours (curated labels, Emojibase labels and tags): `items` holds the already-filtered results, as category groups while browsing and a flat list while searching.
> - The `speak()` count announcements, the `item-press` guard on `onValueChange`, and the scroll reset on each query are gone. The component's own behavior applies: `Status` announces, and `autoHighlight` scrolls the top hit into view.
> - `Autocomplete.Group` / `GroupLabel` / `Row` / `Item` render `grid`, `rowgroup` (labelled by the heading), `row`, and `gridcell`.
> - The input is the Design System `Input` with a search icon prefix and an `Autocomplete.Clear` suffix.
> - Spacing per @fcoveram's review: `gap-sm` between the search field and the skin-tone toggle, no extra space below each row or around the list, and group labels keep the `Autocomplete` inline padding.
> - The popover no longer jumps when it opens or collapses when a search has no results (@mirka's video). The grid's width is held on the list and on the loading state, so the popover keeps one size throughout.
>
> ## Autocomplete notes
>
> @mirka asked to hear about styling difficulties with the current `Autocomplete`. These are the places where the picker still has to add its own styles, plus a couple of behaviors worth documenting. None of them patch the component; they are listed here so they can go back into `Autocomplete` or its docs if that makes sense.
>
> 1. **Inline mode has no width when empty.** With `inline`, nothing gives the list an intrinsic width, so when `Empty` shows (or while loading) the container collapses to the padding and a surrounding popover resizes and repositions. `Popup` has width variants; inline has nothing comparable. The picker sets `min-inline-size` on the `List`.
> 2. **Sticky group labels.** Long grouped lists read better with the heading pinned while its section scrolls. `GroupLabel` has no background, so making it sticky means adding `position: sticky`, a `z-index`, and a background that matches whatever surface it sits on (here the `@wordpress/components` popover's `$white`, which is not a token).
> 3. **Item styles assume a list row.** `Item` brings `margin-inline`, asymmetric inline padding for a leading icon, left alignment, and a `size-md` min height. A grid cell wants a centered square with no padding, so the picker overrides `justify-content`, `height`, `padding`, and `font-size`. The Grid story does the same with inline styles, so a cell size or variant for grid mode might be worth having.
> 4. **Row layout is left to the consumer.** `Row` has no layout styles, so the column template and gap are the picker's. Probably intended, but a line in the docs (or a `columns` option) would help the next grid.
> 5. **Inline scroll container.** The `List` styles are built for `Popup`'s grid areas (`scrollable` / `footer`, and `Empty` uses `grid-area: main`). Inline, the consumer brings its own scroll container, so `scrollbar-gutter` and the `scroll-padding` that keeps a highlighted cell clear of a sticky heading are ours. Documenting `ListBody` as the inline scroll container might cover this.
> 6. **`Status` updates on every keystroke.** The count re-renders in the polite live region per keystroke. The previous version debounced it by 500ms, like the block inserter, so screen readers hear the settled count. Not tested with a screen reader yet; a debounce option or docs guidance could help.
> 7. **Pressing an item writes its value into the input.** `onValueChange` fires with reason `item-press` and the item's string value. Harmless here, since picking closes the popover (in testing the field kept the query until it unmounted), but a picker that stays open would need to filter on `reason`. Worth a note in the docs.
> 8. **Performance with ~1,900 items.** All 1,919 cells mount; rows use `content-visibility: auto`. In headless Chromium on a Mac: open 165-190ms, first keystroke ~40ms, later keystrokes under 20ms, clearing the search ~55ms. No virtualization needed at this size; it was not tried with `grid`.
>
> ## Comparison with #78176
>
> Measured before this round, in headless Chromium against the same wp-env, same Emojibase data (1,919 gridcells), dataset already cached, median of 7 opens, two runs each. Open time is from the click to the painted grid.
>
> | | #78176 (`Composite`) | This PR (`Autocomplete` grid) |
> |---|---|---|
> | Search field to grid | Several Tabs, then roving tabindex | Arrow keys from the field, focus stays in the field |
> | Enter on a search result | Tab into the grid first | Picks the highlighted (top) result |
> | Crosses categories with arrows | Yes | Yes |
> | Input semantics | `searchbox` + separate `grid` | `combobox` with `aria-haspopup="grid"`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant` |
> | Open, median | 329-344ms | 210-274ms |
> | Longest task on open | 245-262ms | 78-112ms |
> | Type one letter ("h") | ~124ms | 67-76ms |
> | Clear the search | 95-98ms | 105-121ms |
>
> Timings move by a few tens of ms between runs, so read them as "not slower" more than as a precise speedup. The numbers after switching to `items` are in note 8 above; they were taken with a different harness, so they are not directly comparable to the table.
>
> ## Risks and open questions
>
> - The search field is a `combobox`, not a `searchbox`. Screen reader testing would be good, especially VoiceOver's reading of the active cell and the `Status` count.
> - Escape closes the whole picker on the first press, even with a query typed.
> - Group headings use the Design System label style (per @mirka) rather than Heading/md from the design spec.
>
> ## Testing Instructions
>
> [![Test in WordPress Playground](https://img.shields.io/badge/Test_in-WP_Playground-blue?style=for-the-badge&logo=wordpress)](https://playground.wordpress.net/gutenberg.html?pr=83538)
>
> 1. Enable Notes, add a note to a block, and click the "Add reaction" button on it. The popover should open at its final size and position, without a jump (easiest to see with scrollbars set to "Always" in macOS settings).
> 2. Without leaving the search field, press ArrowDown, then move around with the arrow keys; the highlight should cross from "Frequently used" into "Smileys & Emotion" and beyond.
> 3. Press Enter; the highlighted emoji is added as a reaction.
> 4. Reopen the picker and type "heart"; the top result is highlighted. Press Enter to add it.
> 5. Type a query with no matches, eg. "zzzq". "No emoji found." shows and the popover keeps its width.
> 6. Tab from the search field; focus moves to the skin-tone button.
>
> Tested: the collab sidebar unit tests (204 pass), and the full `block-notes.spec.js` e2e spec in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit (81 pass). The empty-state e2e test now also checks the popover width; it fails without the width fix (the popover shrank by ~140px).
>
> ## Screenshots
>
> Captured with classic (always visible) scrollbars.
>
> | Open | Arrow key highlight | Search | No results |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | ![Picker open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamsilverstein/gutenberg/issue-assets/issue-assets/pr83538-autocomplete-open-v3.png) | ![Highlight moved with the arrow keys](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamsilverstein/gutenberg/issue-assets/issue-assets/pr83538-autocomplete-keyboard-v3.png) | ![Search for heart, top result highlighted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamsilverstein/gutenberg/issue-assets/issue-assets/pr83538-autocomplete-search-v3.png) | ![No emoji found, popover keeps its width](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamsilverstein/gutenberg/issue-assets/issue-assets/pr83538-autocomplete-empty-v3.png) |
>
> ## Screencast
>
> Opening the picker, arrow keys across categories, searching, the empty state, and picking with Enter (keys shown bottom left): 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cecc184-c7eb-433b-a196-85dac11b1d1f

Fixes #83513

_Claude wrote up the change, summary below:_

> ## What?
>
> Deselect an inline note when the caret moves out of its highlighted text and into plain text in the same block.
>
> ## Why?
>
> Clicking inside an inline note's highlight makes the note active, but clicking elsewhere in the same block left it active. The only way to deactivate it was clicking a different block.
>
> The `core/note` format's `edit` component selected the note when the caret entered the marker, and left clearing to the block-level sync in `notes.jsx`. That sync only runs when the selected block changes, so moving the caret within the block never cleared the note.
>
> ## How?
>
> `NoteFormat` in `collab-sidebar/format.js` now remembers the marker the caret was last in. When the caret leaves it for plain text, it deselects that note, but only if it is still the selected note. A note picked from the sidebar or by the block-level sync is left alone. Leaving the block entirely still goes through the block-level sync, since the format component unmounts then.
>
> Worth noting: when a block has both a block-level note and an inline note, leaving the inline highlight deselects rather than falling back to the block-level note. Picking the "right" block-level note (unresolved first) would need the note records, which the format component doesn't have. Open to changing that if reviewers think the fallback matters.
>
> ## Testing Instructions
>
1. Add a paragraph with some text.
2. Select a word or two and choose "Add note" from the block options menu, then add the note.
3. Click somewhere else in the paragraph, click "Add note" again and add another note
4. At this point, the block has a block level note and a selection note.
5. Click the post title so the note is inactive.
6. Click inside the highlighted text - the note becomes active in the sidebar.
7. Click other text in the same paragraph, outside the highlight - the selection note should become inactive and the block level note should become active. 
8. Click back into the highlight - the selection note is active again.

>
> A new e2e test covers this: `moving the caret out of a marker within the block deselects its note` in `test/e2e/specs/editor/various/block-notes.spec.js`. It fails on trunk and passes with the fix, and the rest of the notes e2e specs pass locally.
>

>

resources.body: ## Summary Closes https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/75144 Adds the foundation for emoji reactions on block notes. This PR is scoped to a small **curated 5-emoji quick row** (heart, celebration, smile, eyes, rocket). The full searchable emoji picker behind a `+` button lives in a [follow-up PR stacked on this one](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/78176) - per [@t-hamano's request](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/76767#issuecomment-4416920752), so library/bundling decisions can be reviewed separately. ### Storage: reactions as a custom comment type Reactions are stored as individual `reaction` comment records (one per user-emoji-note triple), [as suggested by @swissspidy](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/75148#issuecomment-3901554331), in preference to JSON blobs in comment meta: ``` comment_type = 'reaction' comment_parent = comment_content = // e.g. 'heart' user_id = ``` This is more flexible, aligns with WordPress data patterns (similar to the [React plugin](https://wordpress.org/plugins/react/)), and could eventually extend to regular comments. The custom type is hidden from `wp-admin/edit-comments.php` and excluded from comment counts. ### Curated emoji set The default 5 emojis (heart, celebration, smile, eyes, rocket) are stored as ASCII slugs (e.g. `heart`). Storing slugs sidesteps utf8 vs utf8mb4 portability issues on the comments table and gives stable grouping in the `reaction_summary` aggregation. The list is filterable via the `gutenberg_note_reaction_emojis` PHP filter and exposed to clients through the REST API schema (`reaction_emojis` property on `OPTIONS /wp/v2/comments`), implementing the approach [suggested by @Mamaduka](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/75549#issuecomment-3921467462). ### Efficient reaction loading Each note response includes a `reaction_summary` field - `{ [emojiSlug]: { count, reacted, my_reaction_id } }`. The schema lives in [`class-gutenberg-rest-comment-controller-7-1.php`](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/blob/add-notes-emoji-reactions-try-addditional-comment-type/lib/compat/wordpress-7.1/class-gutenberg-rest-comment-controller-7-1.php), populated in `prepare_item_for_response()`. - **No N+1**: `get_items()` pre-fetches summaries for the entire result set with one aggregated `GROUP BY` query plus one query for the current user's own reactions, regardless of how many notes are returned (see `prefetch_reaction_summaries()`). - **Lazy-loaded reactor names**: who reacted is *not* embedded in `reaction_summary` - names are fetched on tooltip hover, so the initial notes load stays cheap. ### Popover architecture The curated picker uses `@wordpress/components/Dropdown`, whose Popover portals to ``. This is essential because the collab sidebar has an `overflow: hidden` chain reaching all the way up to `.interface-interface-skeleton__sidebar` (framework-level); a non-portaled popover would clip. The note thread's `onBlur` handler exempts `.components-popover` so that focus moving into the picker doesn't deselect the note (which would unmount the trigger and close the picker mid-click). ### Where the trigger lives The 😊 trigger floats in the note's top corner, in the same column as Resolve and the actions menu, and stays faded until the note is hovered or the trigger itself is focused. A note nobody has reacted to costs no vertical space for the option, and the note text keeps a safe area on that side so it never runs underneath. Once a reaction lands the row drops into the flow, and the trigger trails the pills and wraps with them. This follows [@annezazu's suggestion](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/78176#issuecomment-5481602877) and [@fcoveram's exploration](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/82324#issuecomment-5538776739), and was first built in #82313 on the follow-up PR before moving here per [@draganescu's question](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/76767#issuecomment-5804509857). - The reveal hangs off the note and the trigger, not the thread. The thread is `tabIndex={ 0 }`, so a thread-level `:focus-within` would hold for as long as the note is selected, and a thread-level `:hover` would reveal the trigger on every note in the thread at once. - The whole treatment sits inside `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch device keeps a trigger it can actually see. - Pills no longer disappear when a note is deselected. Reactions are information about the note rather than one of its actions. - Pill treatment follows the [Notes emoji reaction Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/3dd6oLYd29li43VB12AP2j/Notes-emoji-reaction?node-id=54-4881): your own reaction is a transparent pill with the brand outline, other people's are quiet neutral text, and the trigger is a minimal icon button - all Design System `Button` variants, no custom CSS. ### Related - Previous PR: #75549 - Follow-up: PR for the full searchable picker stacked on this one - #78176 ### Remaining feedback from #75549 - [ ] **Unbounded reaction requests** (@ellatrix) - `useEntityRecords` for reactions has no `per_page` limit. Consider lazy-loading reactions only when a note thread is opened. [Comment](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/75549#discussion_r2800479741) - [ ] **Move emoji SVG icons to `@wordpress/icons`** (@ellatrix) - Low priority, fine for now. [Comment](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/75549#discussion_r2800481125) - [ ] **Reaction embedding** (@Mamaduka) - Reactions could be an embeddable resource on each note to reduce the number of requests. [Comment](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/75549#issuecomment-3912990097) - [ ] **Performance at scale** (@Mamaduka) - Consider how reactions perform with thousands of comments (e.g. make.wordpress.org). [Comment](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/75549#issuecomment-3912990097) ### Already addressed - **Move PHP code to `wordpress-7.1` compat dir** (@Mamaduka, @t-hamano) - Done - **Rename comment type to `reaction`** (@swissspidy) - Done - **Emoji extensibility / filtering** (@Mamaduka, @youknowriad, @aaronjorbin) - `gutenberg_note_reaction_emojis` filter, surfaced via REST schema - **Re-add reaction after removing** - Fixed both server-side (status='approve' duplicate guard) and client-side (force-delete + parent-note refetch); regression-guarded by E2E test - **Full picker scope** (@t-hamano) - Moved to a follow-up [PR](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/78176) stacked on this one ## Screenshots | At rest | Hovered | Picker open | |---|---|---| | | | | | Your reactions and someone else's | Deselected | |---|---| | | | ## Screencast Hover to reveal the trigger, react twice, then deselect the note: ## Testing [![Test in WordPress Playground](https://img.shields.io/badge/Test_in-WP_Playground-blue?style=for-the-badge&logo=wordpress)](https://playground.wordpress.net/gutenberg.html?pr=76767) For testing with multiple users, use the User Switching Plugin - https://wordpress.org/plugins/user-switching/ - [ ] Create a note on a block - [ ] Move the pointer away from the sidebar - the 😊 trigger is hidden, and the note is no taller for carrying it - [ ] Hover the note - the trigger fades in at the note's top right corner, in the same column as Resolve and the actions menu - [ ] Add a reply, then hover one note in the thread - only that note reveals its trigger - [ ] Tab to the trigger with the keyboard - it appears as focus lands on it - [ ] Click 😊 - pick from the curated 5-emoji row; the trigger now trails the pill - [ ] Move the pointer away from the note - with reactions on it, the trigger stays visible at the end of the pills - [ ] Pick the same emoji twice - verify reaction count goes up, not a duplicate - [ ] Remove a reaction by clicking its pill, then add the same emoji back - verify it works (regression for the trash-counts-as-duplicate bug) - [ ] Add multiple different emojis to the same note - [ ] Hover a reaction pill - verify the tooltip shows the reactor names - [ ] Verify your own reaction takes the blue outline, and someone else's stays quiet with no border or fill - [ ] Click the post title to deselect the note - the pills stay, the trigger goes - [ ] Verify the popover doesn't get clipped by the pinned "All notes" sidebar's overflow - [ ] Check wp-admin comments page doesn't show reaction comments - [ ] Check comment counts aren't inflated by reactions - [ ] Verify keyboard accessibility: Enter on smiley opens picker, ArrowDown/ArrowUp navigates, Enter selects, Escape closes - [ ] Run E2E tests: `npm run test:e2e -- test/e2e/specs/editor/various/block-notes.spec.js` - [ ] Run PHP tests: `npm run test:unit:php:base -- --filter=Gutenberg_REST_Comments` ## AI Use Code and description both written with 🤖 Claude Code, with plenty of steering. I will review and test.

## What?
Closes #49697

Adds a "Files" category to the inserter's Media tab for non-media attachments.

## Why?
- The Media tab only showed images, video and audio from the library.
- PDFs, documents and archives were unreachable, which led to requests to disable the tab.
- "Open Media Library" silently filtered to images, so uploaded PDFs vanished from the grid.
- Design agreed on a single catch-all "Files" category instead of disabling the tab.

## How?
- Adds a `files` core media category querying `media_type: application`, listed last.
- Non-playable items render a grey placeholder with the file name, matching DataViews.
- Selecting a file inserts a File block that reuses the existing attachment.
- Widens the "Open Media Library" picker to `application` and `text` types.
- `registerInserterMediaCategory` now accepts `application` and `text` as `mediaType`.
- Files category is hidden when `core/file` can't be inserted.

## Testing Instructions
1. Upload a PDF to the Media Library.
2. Create a new post and open Inserter → Media.
3. Confirm a "Files" tab appears last and lists the PDF.
4. Click the PDF and confirm a File block is inserted.
5. Click "Open Media Library" and confirm the PDF is visible in the grid.
6. Delete all non-media files and confirm the Files tab disappears.

## What?
Follow-up to #83988.

Adding or resolving a note now writes its anchor through `updateNoteAnchor`, the same way delete and restore already do. Before, pressing Undo right after adding a note detached it from its block ("Original block deleted"), and pressing Undo after resolving an inline note restored its highlight.

## Why?
An anchor write is a side effect of a note action, not a user edit, but create and resolve used plain `updateBlockAttributes`, which adds an undo level. Undo can't bring back or remove the note itself, so undoing only the anchor leaves the note and the content out of sync.

## How?
`updateNoteAnchor` skips the undo level but still marks the post as changed. A new `removeInlineNote` util replaces `clearInlineNoteMarker` and the duplicate marker removal in `onDelete`. Resolve now reads `note.blockClientId` instead of scanning all blocks, so `onEdit` takes the note: `onEdit( note, { content, status } )`. Also dropped the dead `getSelectedBlockClientId()` fallback in `onDelete`.

## Testing Instructions
1. Open a saved post with a paragraph block.
2. Select some of the paragraph's text and add a note.
3. Press Cmd/Ctrl+Z. The note keeps its highlight and stays attached to the block.
4. Resolve the note, then press Cmd/Ctrl+Z. The highlight does not come back.
